evaluation_type: frozen synthetic evaluation; no independent label review

assessments.evidence_quote: For security matters, contact our security lead Jae at jae@fictional-f.example.
assessments.reason: The supplier names a security contact and provides an email address.

assessments.evidence_quote: Our approved, written playbook explains how staff detect, contain, and respond to security incidents.
assessments.reason: The supplier explicitly confirms having an approved, written incident response playbook.

assessments.evidence_quote: Every three months, managers check and recertify access privileges for every user.
assessments.reason: Reviewing access every three months satisfies the requirement to review at least annually.

assessments.evidence_quote: Every administrator must enter a password and a one-time code from an authenticator app when signing in.
assessments.reason: The supplier mandates multi-factor authentication for all administrator accounts.

assessments.evidence_quote: Each quarter we restore a backup into an isolated environment and verify that the recovered application works.
assessments.reason: Restoring backups quarterly satisfies the requirement to test restoration at least annually.

assessments.evidence_quote: We have not appointed anyone to handle security questions, and there is no security contact channel.
assessments.reason: The supplier explicitly states that no security contact or channel has been appointed.

assessments.evidence_quote: Our team follows an established incident response process, but none of the process is documented.
assessments.reason: An incident response process explicitly lacking documentation is assessed as partly met.

assessments.evidence_quote: We recertify access for administrators every year. We never review access for other users.
assessments.reason: Access reviews are performed annually for administrators, but user access is not reviewed for other users.

assessments.evidence_quote: Staff administrators must use MFA; contractor administrators are explicitly exempt and use passwords alone.
assessments.reason: MFA covers only some administrator accounts since contractor administrators are exempt.

assessments.evidence_quote: We restore a backup as a test once every eighteen months.
assessments.reason: The restore test frequency is once every eighteen months, which fails the requirement for at least annual testing.

assessments.evidence_quote: We have not specified who handles security questions.
assessments.reason: The supplier explicitly states they have not specified who handles security questions.

assessments.evidence_quote: Section A: We have an approved written incident response plan. Section B: We have no incident response plan or documentation.
assessments.reason: The answer is contradictory because it simultaneously claims to have and not have an incident response plan.

assessments.evidence_quote: Our current answer says all user access is reviewed quarterly. Our current answer also says no user access reviews occur.
assessments.reason: The answer is contradictory and insufficient to decide because it asserts conflicting statements without a resolution.

assessments.evidence_quote: Administrator logins use advanced security controls.
assessments.reason: The answer is vague because advanced security controls do not explicitly specify multi-factor authentication for all administrator accounts.

assessments.evidence_quote: We make backups every night and retain them for ninety days.
assessments.reason: Making backups alone does not establish restore testing.

assessments.evidence_quote: Nobody is responsible for security enquiries and there is no mailbox for them.
assessments.reason: The supplier explicitly states there is no security contact or mailbox.

assessments.evidence_quote: There is neither an incident-handling process nor a written plan.
assessments.reason: The supplier explicitly states that neither an incident-handling process nor a written plan exists.

assessments.evidence_quote: Account permissions are never reviewed.
assessments.reason: The supplier explicitly states that user access is never reviewed.

assessments.evidence_quote: Every administrator signs in with only a password; no second factor is used.
assessments.reason: The supplier explicitly states that multi-factor authentication is not used for administrators.

assessments.evidence_quote: We have never attempted to recover data from any backup as a test.
assessments.reason: The supplier explicitly states that backup restoration testing is never performed.

assessments.evidence_quote: Our security lead Mina handles security questions at mina@fictional-j.example.
assessments.reason: The supplier named a security contact with contact details.

assessments.evidence_quote: Today we have neither a written plan nor an incident response process.
assessments.reason: The supplier explicitly states that they do not have a written plan or incident response process.

assessments.evidence_quote: All user access is reviewed, but we cannot provide the schedule or say when the latest review happened.
assessments.reason: The answer is vague regarding the frequency of the reviews, so it cannot be determined if it occurs at least annually.

assessments.evidence_quote: We require multi-factor authentication for every administrator account.
